🚨🇺🇸 Regulators just shut down Indiana's United Fidelity, the BIGGEST U.S. BANK FAILURE in more than two years...

The FDIC closed the $5.9 billion lender Friday night, and First Citizens, the same bank that bought Silicon Valley Bank's remains in 2023, is taking it over.

Customers keep their money, and all 22 branches reopen Saturday under the new name.

The fine print is ugly.

The FDIC expects to lose $1.83 BILLION from its insurance fund, an unusually high 31% of the bank's assets, and First Citizens demanded a $2.6 billion discount on the loans it took.

Nobody pays that kind of discount for healthy loans. 

One failed bank isn't a crisis, but regulators owe Americans an answer on whether United Fidelity was one bad lender or the first crack in a bigger pile of bad loans.

Source: CNN, FDIC / Writer: Daniel
